title: Signal Fabric: unified tracing hooks, metrics streams, and adaptive pager rules
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Goal: Build a single 'signal fabric' that stitches tracing hooks, metrics/log pipelines, and a new adaptive paging engine to reduce noise while keeping high-fidelity SLO coverage. This ticket focuses on the platform plumbing and policy surface: (1) standard trace attributes and low-overhead hook points for request routing and sampling, (2) consolidated metrics+log streams with transformation rules for fast SLO windowing, and (3) a rule engine that computes burn-rate, applies suppression/aggregation heuristics, and issues pagers only for high-confidence incidents. Success metrics: reduce false positive pages by 40%, surface total burn-rate regressions within 3 minutes, and keep 99.95% metric ingestion availability during rolling upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing SDK exposes two new hook points: pre-dispatch and post-emit for route-level span enrichment
Metrics pipeline supports 1s and 10s rollups for token-latency and error-rate metrics with consistent tags
Burn-rate rule computes per-SLO short-window and long-window rates and triggers synthetic incidents when thresholds are crossed
Pager engine applies topology-aware suppression (service-level dedupe + correlated anomaly scoring) before sending pages
End-to-end test harness reproduces a token-flood scenario and validates paging behavior and dashboard alerts
comments: 2026-03-06: Kickoff meeting — alignment with Product and SRE. Agreed to prioritize low-overhead tracing hooks and a light-weight rule engine first. Action: Diego to propose hook API and perf budget.

2026-03-08: Design trade-off — decided against full-trace capture in platform hooks to avoid 20% p50 latency regressions observed in prototype. We'll capture context IDs + sampling decision; full spans can be pulled asynchronously for debug traces.

2026-03-09: PR opened for hook interface: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1829 — includes pre_dispatch/post_emit signatures, test stubs, and microbenchmarks. Benchmark results attached in PR showing <0.5ms median overhead.

2026-03-10: Metrics pipeline spec uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Signal+Fabric+Metrics+Spec — outlines tag normalization, renaming rules, and 1s/10s rollup mechanics. Note: will reuse existing transform worker from ENG-40221 to reduce implementation time.

2026-03-11: Implemented a first cut of burn-rate calculator in Go. Local sim shows it detects 20% above-baseline in short-window within 90s. Still need to integrate anomaly scorer and topology-aware dedupe.
2026-03-12: SRE review feedback — recommended adding a decaying confidence score and a suppression policy for on-call groups that are already handling an incident. Added to next sprint scope.
2026-03-13: Integration test notes — synthetic probe harness failing intermittently due to metric tag collisions. Created follow-up issue ENG-52410 to dedupe tag keys during ETL.
implementation_notes: Hook design: minimal runtime dependency, implemented as interface with optional adapters for Go/Python/Node SDKs
Sampling: keep platform default sampling at 0.5% for production; allow product teams to override per-route for canary debugging
Metric schema: canonicalize service, route, model_version, region tags. Token-latency and token-error counters are primary signals
Burn-rate algo: compute normalized error/token consumption vs. baseline using EWMA for short-window and sliding-window for long-window
Anomaly detection: ML-based z-score ensemble will run in background; rule engine uses ensemble score + topological correlation to decide paging
Pager routing: maintain per-oncall flood thresholds and an escalate-if-unhandled policy with exponential backoff
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hook overhead increases p50 for latency-sensitive routes. Mitigation: strict perf budget and feature-flagged rollout for 10% of traffic before broader rollout
Risk: Metric ingestion spikes during rollout causing false burn-rate alerts. Mitigation: circuit-breaker in rule engine that disables short-window alerts if ingestion drops below 95%

Risk: Pager suppression hides a real outage for multi-service incidents. Mitigation: correlation engine will lower suppression for high-confidence multi-service anomalies and escalate to SEV if needed
test_plan: Unit tests for hook interface and adapters
End-to-end test that simulates token-flood and verifies burn-rate detection and pager suppression behavior
Chaos test: roll forwarding worker during high-ingest to confirm circuit-breaker behavior
Load test: validate metric pipeline can sustain 50k TPS with 1s rollups on current infra
